result.summary: Sell a fixed-scope Shopify feed cleanup sprint to small DTC merchants with obvious catalog data issues, using objective Merchant Center/Meta feed problems as proof and CobrAMO for payment.
result.opportunity: Small Shopify stores lose sales and ad eligibility when product titles, variants, image mappings, GTIN/MPN fields, URLs and CSV exports are inconsistent; these errors are visible in Google Merchant Center and Meta commerce tools but easy to fix in a bounded, low-friction sprint.
result.target_customer: Small DTC Shopify merchants in Spain/Europe with 30-300 SKUs, an active Google Shopping or Meta catalog, and obvious product-data inconsistencies.
result.offer: A 1-week Shopify feed cleanup sprint: audit up to 100 SKUs, fix titles, variant names, URLs, image references, units, GTIN/MPN, duplicate rows and CSV export quality, then deliver a cleaned feed snapshot, before/after notes and a 1-page QA checklist. Optional expansion for the next SKU batch after validation.
result.price: 149 EUR for up to 100 SKUs; 299 EUR for up to 300 SKUs or full catalog
result.why_now: Google's Merchant Center product data policies explicitly require accurate, complete product information for free listings and Shopping ads, and merchants often do not notice the issues until performance drops. This creates a direct, measurable pain with a clear, short fix and no need to build a broad SaaS.
actions_completed: Reviewed the monetization playbook and the five seeded routes for this round.
Compared the seed routes against recent competitor attempts and current pain patterns in the repository.
Inspected CobrAMO as the payment infrastructure only; no external prospect or customer contact was created.
Researched public e-commerce feed quality and catalog requirements from official merchant docs.

execution_packet.channel: Personalized outreach via the merchant's public Shopify store contact form or owner email, followed by a short sample audit of 3 SKUs and a fixed-price offer; only after a clear public business contact is identified and no spam is used.
execution_packet.subject: Quick catalog audit for your Shopify feed
execution_packet.message: Hi [Name], I noticed a few obvious issues in your Shopify catalog that can hurt Google Shopping or Meta performance: inconsistent product titles, duplicate or mismatched variant naming, image references or missing GTIN/MPN fields. I can do a quick 3-SKU audit and show exactly what needs fixing before you pay. My offer is a fixed-scope cleanup sprint of 149 EUR for up to 100 SKUs, including a cleaned CSV/feed export and a QA checklist. I can send a short sample audit within 24 hours. Reference: RANK-IAMO510. If useful, I can also show the exact issues in your feed with a no-pressure sample.
execution_packet.deliverable: A fixed-scope feed cleanup pack: cleaned CSV or product export, corrected title/variant/image field updates, QA checklist, and a short before/after summary with the specific issues fixed. If the client wants continuation, the next batch is priced separately.

result.differentiation_from_previous: Unlike the recent GBP/review and generic local-SEO attempts, this offer is narrower, more operational and easier to prove: the pain is a specific catalog-data quality issue with official Google/Merchant Center evidence and a direct, bounded deliverable. It avoids app-store complexity, AI-content scaling and broad SaaS sales cycles while keeping the scope focused on a concrete merchant problem.
result.next_step: Identify 15-20 active Shopify stores in Spain/Europe with public product catalogs and obvious title/variant/GTIN inconsistencies; inspect 3-5 SKUs on each site, then send a personalized note with 2-3 concrete issues and the fixed price. If they respond, send a 3-SKU sample audit and close the first 149 EUR cleanup through CobrAMO using reference RANK-IAMO510.
result.notes: Routes considered in this run: #10 multi-source SaaS metrics cockpit (rejected: enterprise sales cycle and weak fit for direct low-cost first sale), #30 SOP/checklist bundle (rejected: less strong direct buyer evidence in this merchant segment), #50 Android ad-supported utility (rejected: app-store monetization and ad account authorization friction), #70 Amazon Associates buyer guides (rejected: slower content and SEO build), #90 e-commerce product-feed cleanup (selected). This strategy stays close to real market evidence and a short validation loop while preserving a clear CobrAMO payment path and RANK-IAMO510 attribution.
